DAMODARAN_BETAS.title: Damodaran, Betas by Sector (US), January 2026
DAMODARAN_BETAS.facts: Drugs (Biotechnology): 496 firms, levered beta 1.14, D/E 13.04%, unlevered beta 1.03, cash 4.20% of firm value, unlevered beta corrected for cash 1.08. Drugs (Pharmaceutical): 228 firms, 0.98 levered, 0.92 cash-corrected.
DAMODARAN_BETAS.limitation: An industry average across sizes and stages; the regression betas behind it are noisy for small single-asset companies, which is why the traded PHVS beta is not used.

DAMODARAN_ERP.title: Damodaran, implied equity risk premium, January 2026 update
DAMODARAN_ERP.locator: 2025 row of the historical implied premium table
DAMODARAN_ERP.facts: Implied ERP 4.23% on a 4.18% T-bond rate (earnings yield 3.97%, dividend yield 1.15%); 4.33% for 2024 and 4.60% for 2023. Mature-market premium 4.23% after removing the 0.23% US default spread.
DAMODARAN_ERP.limitation: A point estimate that moves with the index level; a 50 bp change in the premium moves the CAPM cost of equity by about 55 bp at a 1.08 beta.

DAMODARAN_RATINGS.title: Damodaran, synthetic ratings and default spreads, January 2026
DAMODARAN_RATINGS.facts: Interest coverage below 0.2 maps to D with a 19.00% default spread; 0.8 to 1.25 maps to Caa/CCC at 8.85%; above 8.5 maps to Aaa/AAA at 0.40%.
DAMODARAN_RATINGS.limitation: Built from rated US firms; a pre-revenue company with negative EBIT sits at the bottom of the table by construction. Used only to show that debt is not a realistic funding source.

KROLL_SIZE_2022.title: Kroll Cost of Capital Navigator size premium by CRSP decile, data as of 31 December 2022 (reproduced in a public rate filing)
KROLL_SIZE_2022.facts: Size premium by decile with the largest company in each: decile 5 $3,770m 0.93%; decile 6 $2,365m 1.16%; decile 7 $1,389m 1.37%; decile 10 $218m 4.83%. Pharvaris at $2,183m market cap sits in decile 6.
KROLL_SIZE_2022.limitation: A 2022 table used for a 2026 valuation date because the current Navigator table is subscription-only; Damodaran argues against any size premium, so the 1.16% is a practitioner convention rather than a measured risk.
